title: Always On Top BSOD around display reconfiguration

judgment.rationale: Three dumps show win32kbase stack recursion during repeated display sleep/wake or monitor power changes, and disabling Always On Top stops recurrence. This supports a cautious user-mode mitigation design, but the kernel dump cannot prove one exact callback operation.
evidence: Reported 0x7F double-fault dumps recurse in win32kbase!vUnreferencePdevWorker.
Trigger is repeated display topology/power transitions with Always On Top enabled.
Disabling Always On Top stopped recurrence.
AlwaysOnTop.cpp installs global WinEvent hooks and mutates tracked windows/borders directly from callbacks.
judgment.recommended_action: Approve a guarded display-transition mitigation design, contingent on current-build reproduction and crash-free paired controls.

fix_assessment.rationale: A PowerToys-side mitigation may reduce reentrant window/border activity during display transitions; exact causality remains unconfirmed.

proposed_fixes.title: Quiesce Always On Top during display transitions
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Unconfirmed reentrant interaction between global WinEvent callback work and win32k display-object teardown/recreation during monitor power or topology changes.
plan: Instrument and reproduce the event sequence on current Windows builds with paired enabled/disabled runs.
Detect display/session transition boundaries and temporarily quiesce border refresh and tracked-window mutation.
Coalesce deferred refresh work and resume after the display topology stabilizes, with cleanup-safe hook handling.
Add regression tests for callback reentrancy and manual multi-monitor sleep/wake validation.
verification: Repeat sleep/wake, lock/display-timeout, and monitor power-cycle scenarios.
Confirm no 0x7F recurrence and preserve pin/unpin/foreground behavior.

confidence.rationale: The correlation and callback architecture support a mitigation, but kernel evidence does not identify the exact triggering operation.

issue_context.summary: Always On Top correlates with repeatable win32kbase recursion BSODs during display power/topology changes.
known_information: Three dumps and a disable-module control are reported.
information_gaps: Exact callback/event immediately before the kernel recursion.

design.root_cause: Global hook callbacks can mutate window and border state while win32k is changing display objects.

implementation_steps.change: Add transition-aware quiescing and coalesced deferred refresh rather than mutating borders during display teardown.
Track transition lifecycle and cancel deferred work safely.

verify: Run enabled/disabled paired stress scenarios on current Windows.
Verify normal pin/unpin and foreground updates.
risks: Delayed borders may be briefly stale.
alternatives: Disable Always On Top whenever multiple monitors exist: rejected as excessive behavior change.
Remove all global hooks: rejected because they provide core tracking behavior.

fork_trace.note: Fork-only design mirror; no upstream action implied.

adversarial_review.conclusion: No blocking objections; mitigation must remain conditional and be validated against current dumps/builds.
non_blocking_notes: Do not claim kernel root cause.

actions.label: Approve Always On Top mitigation design
